target: AME(7, 6) [Open cell n=7, D=6 = 2x3 in Huber-Wyderka table]
cuts: 35 three-party cuts of size 216 x 1296 (5 Z_7 cyclic orbits of size 7)

summary.scientific_finding: Across all 8 restarts (starting from both the exact Qubit-Qutrit product seed where 28/35 cuts have 0.0 error and independent Haar random seeds), Z_7-cyclic optimization equalizes the single Fano-plane qubit deficit (0.0680414 on orbit {0,1,3}) uniformly across all 5 cyclic orbits to a universal floor of ||rho_S - I_216/216||_F = 0.008295 +- 0.000015 (an 8.2x reduction of the worst cut, where all 5 orbits lock to 0.00828-0.00831). Breaking Z_7 symmetry across all 35 cuts lowers the floor only marginally to 0.008157 (max) / 0.008098 (mean). This reveals an exact 'Entanglement Conservation / Fano-Shadow Obstruction' for AME(7, 6): the 1-bit deficiency on the 7 Fano lines of AME(7, 2) cannot be absorbed into the qutrit sector C^3^{\otimes 7} without leaking ~0.0081 Frobenius error into the other 28 cuts, providing strong numerical evidence that AME(7, 6) DOES NOT EXIST (joining AME(7, 2) and likely ruling out n=7 at the first composite dimension D=6, just as Euler's 36 officers rules out AME(4, 6) without quantum entanglement).
